---
title: "arg_check(): more examples"
---
<br>

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    error = TRUE, 
    collapse = FALSE,
    comment = "##"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(saferDev)
```
<br>


### Dataset

```{r}
vec1 <- -1:3 # vector of integers.
vec2 <- 1:3 / 3 # vector of positive proportions.
vec3 <- c(1, 2, 3) # vector of positive integers but stored as "double".
vec4 <- "pearson" # vector of characters.
vec5 <- c("a", "b","a", "b") # vector of characters.
mat1 <- matrix(vec1) # matrix of integers.
mat2 <- matrix(c(1:3 / 3, NA)) # matrix of proportions with NA.
```
<br>

### Dataset info

```{r}
vec1 # vector of integers.
vec2 # vector of proportions.
vec3 # vector of integers but stored as "double".
vec4 # vector of characters.
vec5 # vector of characters.
mat1 # matrix of integers.
mat2 # matrix of proportions with NA.
```
<br>

### Simple examples
```{r}
# Check that vec1 is type integer.
arg_check(data = vec1, typeof = "integer")


# Check that vec1 is a vector of type double -> problem because vec1 is not type "double", 
# but type "integer".
arg_check(data = vec1, class = "integer", typeof = "double")


# Check that vec1 is an integer vector of length 3 without negative values and 
# without NA -> problem because of length 5 and negative values inside vec1.
arg_check(
    data = vec1, 
    class = "integer", 
    typeof = "integer", 
    length = 3, 
    neg_values = FALSE, 
    na_contain = FALSE
)


# No result displayed because the output list is assigned to res
# (see below the print argument).
res <- arg_check(data = vec1, typeof = "integer")


# With data = NULL, a problem is reported here because typeof(NULL) is "NULL", not "integer".
arg_check(data = NULL, typeof = "integer")
```
<br>

### Arguments <code>class</code>, <code>typeof</code>, <code>mode</code> and <code>length</code>
The <code>class</code> argument is compared exactly (same values, in the same order) to <code>class(data)</code>: 
matrices have class <code>c("matrix", "array")</code>, and ordered factors have class <code>c("ordered", "factor")</code>. 
The <code>typeof</code> and <code>mode</code> arguments are single strings compared to <code>typeof(data)</code> 
and <code>mode(data)</code>, and <code>length</code> is a single integer compared to <code>length(data)</code>. 
See the help of <code>arg_check</code>.

```{r, echo = TRUE, error = TRUE}
# Example.
arg_check(
    data = vec1, 
    class = "integer", 
    typeof = "integer", 
    mode = "numeric", 
    length = 5
)

# Warning: class, typeof and mode are not checked against each other: each one is compared to the tested object.
# Here, typeof = "integer" and mode = "character" are incoherent: the mode is reported as a problem.
arg_check(
    data = vec1, 
    typeof = "integer", 
    mode = "character"
)

# Bad mode argument value: mode() never returns "integer".
arg_check(
    data = vec1, 
    mode = "integer"
)

# Vector class values are also possible, tested exactly (same values, same order).
# Here, no problem because class(mat1) is c("matrix", "array"), matching exactly the class argument.
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("matrix", "array"), 
    typeof = "integer"
)

# Problem here, because the written values must be identical, element per element, in the same order.
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("array", "matrix"), 
    typeof = "integer"
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>prop</code>
```{r}
# Check for values between 0 and 1 only (neg_values = FALSE).
# With neg_values = TRUE (default), values between -1 and 1 are accepted.
arg_check(
    data = vec2, 
    prop = TRUE, 
    neg_values = FALSE 
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>double_as_integer_allowed</code>
```{r}
# Check for integers, even if numbers are stored as double.
# With double_as_integer_allowed = TRUE, integers stored as double are accepted.
arg_check(
    data = vec3, 
    typeof = "integer",
    double_as_integer_allowed = TRUE
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>options</code>
```{r}
# Check that the values of data are among the options. Here no problem, because vec4 is "pearson", one of the options.
arg_check(
    data = vec4, 
    options = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall")
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>all_options_in_data</code>
```{r}
# Check that data contains all the options, and nothing else.
# Here no problem detected because vec5 contains at least one copy of "a" and "b", and nothing else.
arg_check(
    data = vec5,
    options = c("a", "b"), 
    all_options_in_data = TRUE
)

# Here no problem detected because vec5 is only made of some of the options ("a" and "b").
arg_check(
    data = vec5,
    options = c("a", "b", "c"), 
    all_options_in_data = FALSE
)

# Here a problem is detected because vec5 must contain "a", "b" and "c", at least once each, and nothing else.
arg_check(
    data = vec5,
    options = c("a", "b", "c"), 
    all_options_in_data = TRUE
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>na_contain</code>
```{r}
# Check for the absence of NA.
# Warning: na_contain = TRUE means "no check". Thus, NA can be present or not. 
# Whatever na_contain, data made of NA only always gives an error, as for every argument of the safer-r functions.
arg_check(
    data = mat2,
    prop = TRUE,
    neg_values = FALSE,
    na_contain = FALSE 
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>neg_values</code>
```{r}
# Check for the absence of negative values.
# Warning: neg_values = TRUE means "no check". Thus, negative numbers can be present or not. 
arg_check(
    data = vec1, 
    typeof = "integer",
    neg_values = FALSE
)

# Error: neg_values = FALSE cannot be used if typeof and mode are NULL (and prop is FALSE). 
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("matrix", "array"),
    neg_values = FALSE
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>inf_values</code>
```{r}
# Check for the absence of Inf/-Inf values.
# Warning: inf_values = TRUE means "no check". Thus, infinite numbers can be present or not.
arg_check(
    data = vec2, 
    typeof = "double",
    inf_values = FALSE
)

# Error: inf_values = FALSE cannot be used with typeof = "integer". 
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    typeof = "integer",
    inf_values = FALSE
)

# Error: inf_values = FALSE cannot be used if typeof and mode are NULL. 
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("matrix", "array"),
    inf_values = FALSE
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>print</code>
```{r}
# No message displayed because print is FALSE.
res <- arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = "data.frame",
    print = FALSE
)

# Message displayed. Warning: this is not an error, just a message.
res <- arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = "data.frame",
    print = TRUE
)

# Even if print is TRUE, no message displayed because no problem.
res <- arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("matrix", "array"),
    print = TRUE
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>data_name</code>
```{r}
# Modification of the name of the tested object in the message
arg_check(
    data = vec1, 
    typeof = "integer", 
    data_name = "OBSERVATION_1"
)

# Useful when data is an expression, not an object name.
x <- 1
arg_check(
    data = get("x"), 
    typeof = "integer", 
    data_name = "x"
)

# If "data_name" is not used.
arg_check(
    data = get("x"), 
    typeof = "integer", 
    data_name = NULL
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>data_arg</code>
```{r}
# Message with "argument". Useful when arg_check() is used inside a function to test its arguments.
arg_check(
    data = vec2, 
    typeof = "integer", 
    data_arg = TRUE
)

# Message with "object".
arg_check(
    data = vec2, 
    typeof = "integer", 
    data_arg = FALSE
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>safer_check</code>
```{r}
# Safer checks performed before running.
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("matrix", "array"), 
    safer_check = TRUE
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>lib_path</code>
```{r}
# The "NOTGOOD" path does not exist (lib_path is only checked and used when safer_check is TRUE).
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("matrix", "array"), 
    lib_path = "NOTGOOD"
)
```
<br>

### Argument <code>error_text</code>
```{r}
# Add a text in error messages returned by arg_check().
arg_check(
    data = mat1, 
    class = c("matrix", "array"), 
    lib_path = "NOTGOOD",
    error_text = " === TEXT ADDED ==="
)
```
<br>

### All the arguments
```{r}
arg_check(
    data = vec1, # object to check.
    class = NULL, # check the expected class (tested exactly, same values, same order).
    typeof = "integer", # check the expected type.
    mode = NULL,  # check the expected mode.
    length = NULL,  # check the expected length.
    prop = FALSE,  # check that data is made of proportions?
    options = NULL,  # allowed values of data.
    double_as_integer_allowed = FALSE,  # can integers be stored as double for class = "integer" or typeof = "integer"?
    all_options_in_data = FALSE,  # all the options argument values must be present at least once in the data argument, and nothing else?
    na_contain = FALSE,  # can data contain NA? Only tested if FALSE.
    neg_values = TRUE,  # can data contain negative values? Only tested if FALSE.
    inf_values = TRUE,  # can data contain infinite values? Only tested if FALSE.
    print = FALSE,  # display a message if the $problem output is TRUE?
    data_name = NULL,  # name of the tested object in the returned text.
    data_arg = TRUE,  # If TRUE, "ARGUMENT" is written in output messages, otherwise "OBJECT".
    safer_check = TRUE, # perform some "safer" checks (see https://github.com/safer-r)?
    lib_path = NULL, # where the required packages are if not in the default directories.
    error_text = "" # add information in error messages returned by the function.
)
```
